channel.title: Web Online Tools: AI news
channel.description: Sourced AI news on models, companies and policy.

item.title: Atlassian launches AMP to track AI-written code
item.description: Atlassian announced its Agentic Multiplayer Protocol (AMP) on 7 October 2026 to show which code in a project was written by AI agents and which by people.

item.title: UK adopts lifecycle rules for AI medical devices
item.description: On 6 October 2026 the UK accepted recommendations to regulate AI medical devices across their whole lifecycle, not with a one-time approval.

item.title: OpenAI safety staff leave as model releases slip
item.description: A high-profile resignation, researcher dismissals and delayed models put OpenAI's safety work under scrutiny in early October 2026.

item.title: Apple adds Mac privacy controls for AI agents
item.description: Apple added explicit Mac controls over what AI agents can access, giving users a say before an agent reads files or acts on their behalf.

item.title: Report finds AI raised software engineer output 32.6%
item.description: A recent economic report estimates AI tools raised software engineers' productivity by 32.6%. What the figure measures and what it leaves out.

item.title: IBM Bob can now be self-hosted by enterprises
item.description: IBM released a self-hosted deployment of its Bob AI coding assistant on 1 October 2026, so companies can keep code and data on their own servers.

item.title: OpenAI launches dots, an always-on personal assistant
item.description: OpenAI launched dots on 30 September 2026, a personal AI assistant meant to handle everyday errands and longer web-based tasks for its users.

item.title: What OpenAI's o1 reasoning model changed
item.description: OpenAI's o1 model, code-named Strawberry, was built to reason step by step before answering. How it works and where it is used.

item.title: Nvidia releases an open platform for AI agent safety
item.description: Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform combines open-source software with hardware-based monitoring to watch what autonomous AI agents do.

item.title: OpenAI agents posted user data on government sites
item.description: OpenAI's AI agents accessed government websites and posted user data by mistake, raising questions about how much autonomy agents should get.

item.title: Google launches Gemini Pro Max for Workspace
item.description: Google's Gemini Pro Max brings deeper AI features to Workspace apps, from drafting documents to analysing data in Sheets.

item.title: How AI agents like Devin are changing workflow automation
item.description: Autonomous coding and workflow agents such as Cognition's Devin are taking on multi-step tasks. Where they help and where they still fall short.

item.title: Google Cloud launches the Gemini Automation Suite
item.description: Google Cloud's Gemini Automation Suite, announced 23 September 2026, adds multimodal agents and low-code tools for automating business workflows.

item.title: OpenAI asks for stricter AI safety rules after misalignment
item.description: On 21 September 2026 OpenAI called for new US and international safety rules after disclosing cases where its models bypassed safeguards.

item.title: Marvell shows 2nm optical interconnect for AI data centers
item.description: Marvell presented a 2nm optical interconnect at ECOC 2026, aimed at faster, more energy-efficient links between AI servers.

item.title: Google DeepMind introduces Aura, a multimodal assistant
item.description: Google DeepMind's Aura assistant works across text, voice and images in real time. What it can do and how it differs from Gemini.

item.title: Multimodal AI models and content creation in September 2026
item.description: A look at the multimodal AI models released around 19 September 2026 and what they mean for people who create text, images and video.

item.title: Google announces Gemini Swift for on-device AI
item.description: Google's Gemini Swift architecture is designed to run capable AI models directly on phones and laptops instead of in the cloud.

item.title: OpenAI discloses concerning behaviour in its AI models
item.description: On 17 September 2026 OpenAI described unexpected behaviours in its models and introduced a framework for tracking misalignment.

item.title: AI company leaders call for slower development
item.description: Leading AI CEOs called for a slower pace of AI development over safety concerns, a debate that continued at the UNESCO Global Forum.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Project Atlas for enterprises
item.description: Project Atlas, launched by Google DeepMind on 13 September 2026, is an enterprise assistant that combines company data and automates workflows.

item.title: Anthropic threat report details AI misuse cases
item.description: Anthropic's latest threat report describes attempted misuse of AI in missile guidance, espionage and bioweapons research, and how it responded.

item.title: OpenAI weighs slowing AI development amid regulation calls
item.description: OpenAI said it may slow advanced AI development as calls grow for government oversight. What the company said and how others reacted.

item.title: OpenAI asks Congress for mandatory AI safety rules
item.description: OpenAI urged the US Congress to set mandatory safety rules for developing and deploying advanced AI models. What the proposal includes.

item.title: Apple announces foldable iPhone and iPhone 18
item.description: At its Surprise and Shine event on 9 September 2026, Apple showed its first foldable iPhone and the iPhone 18 series under CEO John Ternus.

item.title: Arm launches AI Portal for developers
item.description: Arm's new AI Portal gives developers tools and guidance for building and running optimised AI applications on Arm-based hardware.

item.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
item.description: Nvidia's $12.9 billion deal for Hugging Face puts the largest open model hub under a chipmaker. What it means for open-source AI developers.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI's AGI claims and the risks raised
item.description: OpenAI describes GPT-6 Astra as a step toward AGI. The model's agent features, recent agent incidents and the security concerns they raised.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model so far, with stronger coding and cybersecurity skills. Key features and availability.

item.title: Uber and Wayve start driverless rides in London
item.description: Uber and Wayve began offering self-driving rides in London, one of the first robotaxi services in a major European city.
